candidate.subject: Casimir d'Almeida (Albert-Kahn spelling: Casimir d'Alméida)
candidate.role_fit: The 1936 Dahomeyan Administrative Council election record names Casimir d'Almeida as the elected Porto-Novo councillor. This is a period governing representative role, not proof that he was a colony-wide head of state or an independent Dahomey president.
candidate.1936_capability: Exact 1936 council membership is documented by the captured election record, while the archival portrait is dated 11 July 1931. The package must use a council or provisional-government role, not an invented national-leader title.

source.place: Boulogne, property of Albert Kahn; collection record associates the subject with Benin/Dahomey

delegation_record.identity_and_role: The Albert-Kahn description identifies Casimir d'Almeida as a Dahomeyan delegation member and homme politique (politician).

role_record.result: The record says three Administrative Council members were elected from Abomey, Ouidah, and Porto-Novo and lists Casimir d'Almeida as the Porto-Novo winner.
role_record.cited_work: Patrick Manning, Slavery, Colonialism and Economic Growth in Dahomey, 1640-1960, Cambridge University Press, 2004, p. 273
role_record.limitation: No primary council minute or independently archived 1936 portrait was located in this gate.

rights.albert_kahn_record: The archive page states operator/employee copyright and freely reusable CC-BY-4.0.
rights.commons_record: The Commons page and API state CC BY-SA 4.0 for the imported original and credit the Albert-Kahn record.
rights.recommended_runtime_basis: If the parent accepts this source, use the Commons CC BY-SA 4.0 basis with attribution to Chevalier Georges, Musée départemental Albert-Kahn, and the Commons record, while retaining the archive CC-BY-4.0 discrepancy in the manifest.
rights.runtime_redistribution: blocked until the parent records the accepted licence basis, attribution text, and share-alike treatment

review.verdict: The manual crop contains one visible subject in a head-and-shoulders frame, excludes the source plate markings, and preserves the archival pixels. It is a source review only and is not a final HOI4-style portrait.
